images.title: An American industrial city around 1900
images.description: Six lessons, the whole Gilded Age in one sitting: the nation the industrial explosion built.

images.title: Andrew Carnegie around 1900
images.description: Carnegie: vertical, owned everything. An alternate portrait for the cram.

images.title: John D. Rockefeller around 1900
images.description: Rockefeller: horizontal, bought everyone. An alternate portrait for the cram.

images.title: A Carnegie steel mill around 1900
images.description: Vertical integration in steel: the trust was Rockefeller's invention, 1882.

images.title: The Standard Oil trust
images.description: The trust was Rockefeller's invention, 1882; then the Sherman Act outlawed trusts in 1890.

images.title: Standard Oil's Broadway headquarters
images.description: Standard Oil became a holding company; its first victims were strikers, the Pullman injunctions leaned on it.

images.title: A Bessemer converter at work
images.description: The loop: railroads needed steel rails; Bessemer's 1856 process made steel cheap; cheap steel built more railroads.

images.title: The Knights of Labor in the 1880s
images.description: The Knights took everybody and hated strikes; the AFL took skilled men only and would walk out.

images.title: Samuel Gompers in the 1890s
images.description: Gompers's AFL: skilled craftsmen only, exclusivity as strategy.

images.title: Haymarket Square after the 1886 bombing
images.description: Eight anarchists convicted on scanty evidence, four hanged; the Knights took the blame anyway.

images.title: Homestead Steel Works in 1892
images.description: Summer 1892: Carnegie's steelworks, Frick in charge, the Pinkertons by barge, the workers beating them back.

images.title: Pennsylvania militia in 1892
images.description: Homestead was Pennsylvania's state militia, about eight thousand Guardsmen; federal troops were 1877 and Pullman.

images.title: Pullman, Illinois, in 1894
images.description: Pullman, 1894: Debs's boycott stopped the railroads; Washington broke it with injunctions and federal troops.

images.title: Eugene Debs in the 1890s
images.description: Debs's boycott, the injunctions leaning on the Sherman Act, In re Debs 1895 blessing it.

images.title: Union cigar makers in the 1890s
images.description: Skilled cigar makers nobody can replace: strike, because the boss can't swap them by morning.

images.title: Italian immigrants around 1900
images.description: The new wave: Italian, Russian, Polish, Catholic and Jewish; about twenty-eight million between 1870 and 1920.

images.title: Ellis Island around 1900
images.description: The front door opened January 1, 1892, not 1890; Angel Island, 1910, was Ellis in reverse.

images.title: Angel Island's barracks
images.description: Ellis processed; Angel detained and interrogated, aimed above all at the Chinese.

images.title: The Chinese Exclusion Act era
images.description: Signed May 6, 1882: Chinese labor immigration suspended for ten years, laborers only, Congress renewing it.

images.title: Immigrants landing in the 1880s
images.description: The other law nobody remembers: the fifty-cent head tax per arriving non-citizen, barring convicts and the ill.

images.title: An 1890s nativist cartoon
images.description: The APA, 1887: anti-immigrant, anti-Catholic; and the Immigration Restriction League, 1894, with its literacy test.

images.title: Gold and the gold standard in the 1890s
images.description: Washington capped the money supply with gold while harvests grew: prices fell, fixed debts got heavier.

images.title: A Kansas farmer in the 1890s
images.description: A thousand dollars at eight percent, wheat prices falling: the debt gets heavier.

images.title: Sharecroppers in the 1890s South
images.description: The crop-lien system: borrow for seed in spring, promise the fall crop, debt rolling forward forever.

images.title: A wheat harvest in the 1890s
images.description: Deflation turns borrowed dollars into boulders: the dollars repaid worth more than the dollars borrowed.

images.title: A Grange meeting in the 1880s
images.description: The Grange, 1867: co-ops and Granger Laws; then the Alliances, a million Southern, two million Plains, a million Colored.

images.title: A Farmers' Alliance rally around 1890
images.description: The trap: same enemies, separate doors; four million farmers split on the color line.

images.title: Silver dollars of the 1890s
images.description: The classic trap: free coinage, the mint stands open, silver in, silver dollars out; debt relief in a silver suit.

images.title: An illustration from The Wizard of Oz
images.description: Dorothy's silver shoes, the Scarecrow as the farmer, the Cowardly Lion as Bryan: the memory device.

images.title: William Jennings Bryan in 1896
images.description: Bryan, thirty-six, the Cross of Gold, fusion with the Populists; McKinley and Hanna's money machine, 271 to 176.

images.title: Homesteaders on the plains
images.description: Homesteaders: 160 acres, ten dollars, Homestead Act 1862; Exodusters out of the South; miners; ranchers.

images.title: Cowboys on a long drive
images.description: Up to a third of the real cowboys were Mexican or African American, which the John Wayne version leaves out.

images.title: Buffalo on the plains
images.description: The reservations: the buffalo destroyed, the tribes on rations; the ground being cleared.

images.title: The Little Bighorn battlefield
images.description: June 1876: the Sioux and Cheyenne wiped out Custer's Seventh, a battlefield victory, a war lost.

images.title: Allotment under the Dawes Act
images.description: 1887: allotments, and the 'surplus' sold to white settlers; allotment on paper, land loss in practice.

images.title: The Carlisle Indian School
images.description: Carlisle, 1879: the boarding schools that tried to erase the culture and save the child.

images.title: Frederick Jackson Turner in the 1890s
images.description: 1893: Turner reads the missing frontier line as the closing of a great historic movement.

images.title: The 1890 census frontier map
images.description: The verb that decides it: the census said the line disappeared; 'closed' is Turner's word.

images.title: The Legacy of Conquest
images.description: Credit Turner for asking it, then list everybody he left out: Limerick, 1987, the West as conquest.

images.title: Alfred Thayer Mahan in the 1890s
images.description: The stack: the 1893 panic and the hunt for markets; Mahan, 1890, sea power; the missionaries; Beveridge.

images.title: American warships in 1898
images.description: The stack: one cause alone is a wrong answer in a confident suit.

images.title: The USS Maine in 1898
images.description: 'Spain sank it': legend. The cause is still open; the leading theory is a boiler failure.

images.title: The Treaty of Paris, 1898
images.description: Cuba free; the Philippines, Guam, Puerto Rico for twenty million; the Senate ratifying by a single vote.

images.title: John Hay in 1898
images.description: The mix-up: 'a splendid little war' was the Spanish-American War of 1898, fewer than four hundred combat deaths.

images.title: Cuba under the Platt Amendment
images.description: Forced into Cuba's constitution: no treaties without American approval, intervention when necessary, Guantanamo.

images.title: A steelworks in 1900
images.description: Box one: the integration machines; Carnegie owned every stage, Rockefeller bought, squeezed, or starved rivals.

images.title: A labor strike in the 1890s
images.description: Box two: Haymarket, the Knights blamed for a bomb they didn't throw; Homestead's state militia; Pullman's troops.

images.title: A Chinatown in the 1890s
images.description: Box three: 1882, laborers only, ten years, renewed and renewed; Ellis 1892 processed, Angel 1910 detained.

images.title: A Populist rally in the 1890s
images.description: Box four: deflation, the railroad, the crop-lien; Omaha 1892; 1896, McKinley 271 to 176; the platform won.

images.title: Western pioneers in the 1880s
images.description: Box five: homesteaders, Exodusters, miners, ranchers; Little Bighorn; Dawes 1887; Turner 1893; Limerick 1987.

images.title: The American empire around 1900
images.description: Box six: the panic, Mahan, the missionaries, Beveridge; the Maine's unproven cause; Teller promised, Platt leashed.

images.title: Senator John Sherman
images.description: Q1: the Sherman Act changed almost nothing at first; the courts ruled manufacturing wasn't interstate commerce.

images.title: The 1890 census bulletin
images.description: Q2: the verb; the census reported the line gone, Turner supplied 'closed.'

images.title: The Cuban flag
images.description: Q3: 1898, the Teller Amendment, no annexation; 1901, the Platt Amendment, the leash.

images.title: A Carnegie steel plant
images.description: Q4: Carnegie integrated vertically, owning every stage; Rockefeller horizontally, buying rival refineries.

images.title: A union meeting in the 1890s
images.description: Q5: scarcity; a skilled craftsman can't be swapped by morning, so his strike hurts.

images.title: Chinese laborers in the 1880s
images.description: Q6: laborers only, for ten years; Washington had never shut the door on a nationality before.

images.title: A reservation during the allotment era
images.description: Q7: the Dawes Act carved reservations into allotments and sold the 'surplus' to white settlers.

images.title: The wreck of the Maine
images.description: Q8: the cause was never conclusively explained; the yellow press declared Spain guilty because guilty sold papers.

images.title: The Capitol in 1913
images.description: Q9: the graduated income tax, the Sixteenth; direct election of senators, the Seventeenth; both 1913.

images.title: The Philippine-American War
images.description: Q10: two wars, two death tolls; the summer war won the empire, the Philippine war showed the cost.

images.title: The campaign of 1896
images.description: Fast bonus: McKinley, 271 to 176; dead party, winning platform.

images.title: The American flag in 1900
images.description: Six lessons, one sitting, most of the traps defused: next, the Progressives.

images.title: Knights of Labor members in the 1880s
images.description: The big tent: more members, more muscle? Numbers lose; leverage wins.

images.title: State militia at Homestead, 1892
images.description: State militia: Maya set the trap and walked straight into it.

images.title: Skilled workers on strike in the 1890s
images.description: Scarcity beats headcount: the boss can't swap them by morning.

images.title: Ellis Island before its 1892 opening
images.description: Ellis Island, 1890: the date that catches everybody; the door opened January 1, 1892.

images.title: A Kansas wheat farmer facing debt
images.description: A thousand dollars at eight percent, wheat prices falling: what happens to the debt?

images.title: Students studying around 1900
images.description: Ten questions, AP-shaped: say your answer before Maya gives it.
